Definition: Beth-Millo, the name of two citadels
BiblicalUsage: Beth-Millo means house of the rampart, and it is named at Shechem, in the crowning of Abimelech. In Judges 9:6 all the men of Shechem and the house of Millo went and made Abimelech king by the oak at Shechem, and in Judges 9:20 Jotham's curse calls down fire on the house of Millo if they dealt falsely with Jerubbaal. The name never stands as a single word in the Hebrew text; it comes as two words, house and Millo, joined together.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Jotham's curse is the whole story of Beth-Millo: a crown made in a hurry, and a fire promised for the men who made it.
